main_text.p: Genef.46.3. à יָד. Chald. Fut. יִתְּנוּן Dabunt,Esr.4.13. תִּנָּה Trades,Elr.7.20. יְתִנָּה Tradet illud, Dan.4.14. Infinit. לְמִתֵּן Ad tradendum,Efræ 7.20. Niph. יִתֵּן Dari, Concedi, Tradi, Reddi, Poni, Disponi, &c. Præter. נָתַן־לָהּ Datur ei,Lev.19.20. נִתְּנוּ Disposita sunt, Ezech.32.23. Hoph.Futur. וְכִי יִתַּן מַיִם Sed si imponatur aqua, Lev.11.38. וַיִּתַּן Ut positum esset, 2.Sam.18.9.
יִתָּן m. Donum, quasi Datum dicas, Proverb.19.6. Aff. מַתְּנָם Donum eorum, Num.18.11.

מַתָּנָה f. Idem, Num.18.6. Constr. כְּמַתְּנַת יָדוֹ Secundum donum manus suæ, Deut.16.17. Plural. מַתָּנוֹת Dona,Gen.25.6. Constr. מַתְּנוֹת Exod.28.38. Aff. בְּמַתְּנוֹתָם Cum donis ipsorum, Ezech.20.26. Chald. Plural. מַתְּנָן Dona, Dan.2.48. Aff. מַתְּנָתֶךָ Dona tua, Dan.5.17.
מַתָּנֶת [?] f. Idem, 1.Reg.13.7. Constr. מַתַּת אֱלֹהִים Donum Dei, Eccles.3.13.

נְתִינִים Nethinæi, servi publici erant, publicis angariis obeundis in domo Dei pro toto cætu Dediti, quasi Deditiii [?] dicti: primùm quidem Gibeonitæ fuerunt à Jehosua ordinati, Josh.9.21. postmodum à Davide ad ministerium Levitarum dediti, Esr.8.20. Vide Kimchi 2.Sam.21.1. & Josh.9. v.2. & Aben Efram Esr.2.43. Chald. נְתִינֵיָא Nethinæi, Esræ 7.24.
נָתַם Diruit, Destruxit: Præterit. נְתַתּוּ נְתִיתָם Destruunt semitam meam, Job.30.13. Convenit cum sequenti verbo.

נָתַץ Diruit, Destruxit, Demolitus est: Præterit. נִתְּצוּ אֶת־מִזְבֵּחַ Diruit altare, Jud.6.v.31. נִתְּצוּ Destruxerunt,2.Reg.25.10. Niph.Præter. נִתְּצוּ Destructæ sunt urbes ejus, Jerem.4.26. Pih.Præter. נִתַּץ Destruxit, 2.Paral.33.3. וַנִּתְּצוּ Et destruent, Ezech.16.39. וְנִתְּצָם Et diruetis, Deut.12.3. Futur. וַיִּנְתֹּץ Et destruxit,2.Par.34.7. וינתצו

page.notes: Hebrew and Greek forms are copied from the scan at reduced resolution; vowel points and dagesh marks in the Hebrew are uncertain throughout and should be checked against a higher-resolution image. "Deditiii" is marked doubtful. The top-line fragment "Genef.46.3." continues an entry from the previous page. The Hebrew word at the start of the Niph. entry for נתם is printed in a larger type; it is transcribed as running text. The Hebrew line "וינתצו" closes the נתץ entry and is kept in the same paragraph.
